summary: Built the Nightfall home page top to bottom as full-width sections. Navigation carries the wordmark, section labels, a segmented theme toggle and a Book time button. The hero pairs a night-sky image with the headline, a one-line description and a four-part new-moon countdown panel. The finder has a region menu, an aperture menu, Bortle chips including All, a right-aligned result count and six observatory cards named after real dark-sky sites. Pricing shows three tiers with a Monthly/Yearly segmented control; prices are drawn as an em dash because no rates were supplied. The booking section pairs a site picker with a December 2026 Monday-first calendar and a slot panel holding six UTC hour slots, a selection line, a running total and a Reserve button. Below that sit the testimonial carousel with prev/next controls and three dots, a six-question FAQ with the first answer open, the newsletter block with an email field, Subscribe button and hidden validation hint, and a three-column footer. One page-wide behaviour describes the sticky nav, theme switch, countdown, finder filtering, billing toggle, booking total, keyboard carousel, single-open accordion and inline email check; it is attached to the boundary because new layers get their ids from Desegnos. The copy and tier prices still need confirmation before launch.

requests.explanation: Built the whole Nightfall home page as nine full-width sections stacked down the page: sticky navigation with theme toggle, hero with live new-moon countdown, observatory finder with region, aperture and Bortle filters plus result count, three-tier pricing with a billing-period switch, a booking widget with observatory picker, December 2026 calendar, hour slots and running total, a testimonials carousel with arrows and dots, a six-item FAQ with one answer open, a newsletter form with inline validation hint, and a footer. Page-wide behaviour is attached to the boundary because new layers receive their ids from Desegnos.

images.prompt: Very dark night-sky photograph: the silhouette of a single domed observatory on a bare ridge beneath the Milky Way, deep navy and ink black tones, one faint warm amber glow escaping the dome slit, no people, no text, no logos, long exposure, fine film grain.

decisionProposals.value: Tier prices are drawn as an em dash with the billing unit beside them; real rates should replace the dash once approved.
decisionProposals.rationale: Prices are a private commercial fact that was not supplied, so the layout reserves the type scale and position for them without inventing numbers.

criticism.message: The three testimonial quotes are representative copy, not real customer statements, because no approved quotes were supplied.
criticism.suggestion: Replace the quote and attribution strings inside the testimonial card with verified customer statements before launch.

criticism.message: Tier prices render as an em dash because no rate card was provided and prices must not be invented.
criticism.suggestion: Supply the real hourly and yearly rates for Stargazer, Observer and Deep Field, then replace the price text and let the Monthly/Yearly control swap the figures.

criticism.message: Hour-slot times, telescopes per site and Bortle ratings per site are structural product detail, not verified site data.
criticism.suggestion: Confirm each site's aperture, Bortle class and available UTC slots, then correct the card meta lines and slot labels.
